deep.reconstruction:
The page is written upside down on the back of a 'DATASETS PICTURES' printout and is crossed out with diagonal strokes. It is a scratch computation, and much of the handwriting is illegible, so what follows is a plausible reading rather than a certain one.

Current context: the notes study systems of pseudo-lines in the disc. The previous page speaks of 'half-circuits around points of order 1, 2 or 0', i.e. orbifold or cone points of a disc-type quotient. On this page Grothendieck uses three generators x0, x1, x2. These are almost certainly the three flag involutions of the 2-dimensional cartographic group (the triangle-type group sigma0, sigma1, sigma2 of the Esquisse d'un programme). In that group sigma_i^2 = 1 and (sigma0 sigma2)^2 = 1.

The NB on the page fits this reading. One defining relation, carried by x0x2, is the incidence condition: each edge has two ends. The other, carried by x0x1, is the 'angle' or valency condition, which fixes the order of the rotation around a vertex or face.

The columns of 0/1 triples look like images of x0, x1, x2 in (Z/2)^3, i.e. characters of the group into {±1}. The test case is x0 -> (1,1,0), x1 -> (1,0,1), x2 -> (1,1,1). In every row the first coordinate is 1, which is the orientation character: each reflection reverses orientation. The other coordinates are characters that may or may not factor through a given quotient.

He then generalises to (1, eps-bar, 0), (1, eps, 0), (1, eta, 1). Here eps is in {±1}, and eps-bar is eps read mod 2 (additive notation). The jottings 'eps - 1' and '1 - 2 = 1' are checks mod 2.

The target groups are the monodromy (automorphism) groups of regular n-gon maps, written T -> D_{2n}. For n even he writes T -> D_{2n} x {±1}, noting a relation with D_n x {±1}. This matches the standard fact that D_{2n} is isomorphic to D_n x Z/2 when n/2 is odd.

The conclusion is read off from the abelianisation of the dihedral group, which is (Z/2)^2 for n even and Z/2 for n odd:
- for n even, the images of x0 and x1 are independent characters (the 'n pair 1 0 / 1 i alpha' rows);
- for n odd, x0 and x1 have the same image (the 'n impair 1 0 0 x0' row), forcing eps = 1;
- x0 and x2 are always independent.

The phrase 'connexion fondamentale ... sur D_2' suggests he wants the canonical double covers, i.e. characters, of the 'fundamental connection' on the disc model. These would serve the orientation and local-system bookkeeping of the pseudo-line configurations, perhaps tied to the U(E) / R(E) construction noted mid-page.

In short, this is a routine computation of Z/2-characters (abelianisation) of cartographic and dihedral groups attached to n-gons, done to decide which double covers or sign systems exist.
errors: Nothing demonstrably wrong; the parity statements (abelianisation of D_{2n} is (Z/2)^2 for n even and Z/2 for n odd) are standard and consistent with the text.
The reading is uncertain because much of the handwriting is illegible; the identification of the 0/1 triples as characters is an interpretation.

deep.surprise_reason: A crossed-out scratch computation of parity and character conditions for dihedral quotients of the cartographic group within the pseudo-line project. The mathematics is elementary and standard; at most it documents Grothendieck applying cartographic-group formalism to pseudo-line arrangements in 1983–84, which is already known from the archive's description.
transcription_corrections: The 0/1 triples are best read as images of x0, x1, x2 (rows), e.g. x0 -> 1 1 0, x1 -> 1 0 1, x2 -> 1 1 1, with the generalised version 1 eps-bar 0 / 1 eps 0 / 1 eta 1.
'eps-bar = eps^{-1} mod 2' is more likely 'eps-bar = eps read (reduced) mod 2', i.e. the additive version of eps in {±1}.
The NB line probably reads: 'la condition d'incidence porte sur x0x2, la condition "angles ..." sur x0x1'.
'T -> D_{2n}' and 'D_n x {±1}' concern the regular n-gon monodromy (dihedral) group; the 'n pair' and 'n impair' cases are contrasted.
